name: Cathedral Basilica of St. Augustine
style: Spanish Colonial, with Renaissance Revival additions
history: St. Augustine was founded by Spain in 1565, and its parish is the oldest Christian congregation in the contiguous United States. Several earlier churches were lost to fire, raids and decay. The present church was built between 1793 and 1797 and is a U.S. National Historic Landmark.
arch: The facade mixes Spanish mission features (curving bell gables, clay roof tiles, a statue niche) with Neoclassical ones. After a fire in 1887 the coquina-stone walls were saved, and architect James Renwick Jr. rebuilt the church and added a Spanish Renaissance-style bell tower.
features: It was designated a U.S. National Historic Landmark in 1970.
An early church of straw and palmetto burned down in 1599.

look.d: Curving bell gables like this are a Spanish mission signature.
A clock looks out over the old plaza of America's oldest European city.

fun: The congregation is older than any English settlement in North America.
journal: 1565. Before Jamestown, before Plymouth. Coquina walls warm in the Florida sun.
